correctness.rationale: A polynomial proof of the classical pedal-area identity and the barycentric identity Q=(a1 λ2λ3+a2 λ3λ1+a3 λ1λ2)/4 work for all positive-area triangles. Exact Dirichlet integrals yield μ=e1/48 and ν=(e1²−e2)/1440. Heron and circumradius formula give e3=4e2−e1², which together with Vieta and SSS proves all-triangle inversion including repeated roots and obtuse cases. Two explicitly constructed isosceles triangles establish that one moment fails. The independent exact rational checker verifies projection and moment identities in acute, right and obtuse examples; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: The two scalar moments of the canonical pedal construction furnish a natural, scale-free and provably minimal inverse measurement of triangle shape. A geometric circumcircle constraint unexpectedly replaces a third statistical moment; the exact cubic and explicit non-similar one-moment collision expose a meaningful boundary compared with centroidal radial and interpoint-distance tomography. No noisy estimation or larger-dimensional claims are made.
